class.name: ClapPluginEffect
class.brief_description: Runs a CLAP audio plugin as an effect on an audio bus.
class.description:
Hosts a [url=https://cleveraudio.org]CLAP[/url] audio plugin, such as a reverb, a compressor or a vocoder, as an effect on an [AudioServer] bus. The plugin processes the bus's audio exactly as Godot's built-in effects do. In the editor, every installed CLAP effect appears in the Audio panel's [b]Add Effect[/b] menu under its own name, such as [code]Clap_DragonflyHallReverb[/code]. Choosing one adds a [ClapPluginEffect] with [member plugin_path] already set. Selecting the effect on a bus opens the plugin's own window (see [method open_editor]). Each of the plugin's parameters appears in the inspector as a slider under [b]Parameters[/b], with the plugin's own text for its value. From a script, use [method find_parameter], [method set_parameter] and [method get_parameter_text]. Parameter changes are sample-accurate: they keep their exact spacing in time and are heard one audio block after they are made. [method set_parameter_at] schedules a change ahead. Two things are saved with the scene: [member plugin_state], the plugin's complete state, and [member param_values], the parameters set by hand. A scene refers to the plugin by its path relative to a plugin folder, so it opens on any machine that has the plugin; where the plugin is missing, the effect passes audio through unchanged. [codeblock] var reverb = ClapPluginEffect.new() reverb.plugin_path = "DragonflyHallReverb.clap" AudioServer.add_bus_effect(AudioServer.get_bus_index("Reverb"), reverb)
var size = reverb.find_parameter("Size") reverb.set_parameter(size, 40.0) print(reverb.get_parameter_text(size)) # The plugin's own text, e.g. "40 m". [/codeblock] [b]Plugin folders:[/b] plugins are found in the folders listed in [code]audio/plugin_host/clap/search_paths[/code] in Project Settings (default [code]res://bin/clap[/code]), then in the system's CLAP folders ([code]CLAP_PATH[/code], [code]~/.clap[/code], [code]/usr/lib/clap[/code] on Linux). The system folders are searched in the editor, and when the game is run from it, if [code]audio/plugin_host/clap/use_system_paths[/code] is on (the default); in an exported game only if [code]use_system_paths_in_exports[/code] is on (off by default). On export, the project's plugin folders are copied to [code]bin/clap[/code] next to the game's executable, since a plugin cannot be loaded from inside a [code].pck[/code] file, and the export warns about each effect whose plugin is in none of them. [b]Note:[/b] Godot runs one instance of an effect per stereo channel pair of a bus, so on a surround bus the plugin runs several times. Parameter changes reach every instance. [b]Note:[/b] Plugin windows open in the editor and in running games (exported ones too), on Linux (X11, or XWayland on Wayland desktops), Windows and macOS. On macOS the plugin is not given the editor's display scale: macOS scales plugin windows for Retina screens itself.

method.name: cancel_learn
method.description: Stops waiting for a controller to learn.

method.name: clear_crashed_plugin
method.description: Lets the plugin at [param path] load again after a crash ([method get_crashed_plugins]); with no [param path], every one.

method.name: clear_midi_map
method.description: Removes every controller mapping.

method.name: close_editor
method.description: Closes the plugin's window, if it is open, and emits [signal editor_closed].

method.name: find_parameter
method.description: Returns the id of the parameter with this display name, such as [code]"Output Gain"[/code], or [code]-1[/code] if the plugin has none. Ids, not names, are what the other parameter methods take: a plugin keeps its ids stable across versions, while names may change.

method.name: get_active_instance_count
method.description: Returns how many of this effect's instances are running the plugin. Godot creates one instance per stereo channel pair of each bus the effect is on (see [method get_instance_count]). A new instance can pass audio through for a frame or two while its plugin is being created, unless a spare was ready (see [member spare_instances]).

method.name: get_crashed_plugins
method.description: The plugins that crashed the program (the editor or a game) while their own code was running: their paths. Such a plugin is not loaded again (its [method get_load_error] says why) until its file changes (an update), or [method clear_crashed_plugin]. One list for CLAP and VST3, kept in Godot's per-user config folder.

method.name: get_dsp_load
method.description: What the plugin costs: the time its processing takes, in percent of the audio's real time, averaged over about a second and summed over its running instances (an effect Godot runs per channel pair counts each). 100 means the plugin alone would make the audio miss its deadline. Cheap to call; measured on the audio thread around each processing call.

method.name: get_dsp_peak
method.description: The worst single block since the last call, in percent of its real time: the spikes [method get_dsp_load] averages away. Reading it starts a new peak.

method.name: get_frames_processed
method.description: Returns the total number of audio frames processed by all of this effect's instances. Useful to check whether the bus is running at all.

method.name: get_instance_count
method.description: Returns how many instances of this effect Godot has created: one per stereo channel pair of each bus the effect is on. [code]0[/code] means the effect is on no bus.

method.name: get_load_error
method.description: Returns why the plugin could not be loaded, or an empty string if it loaded (or no [member plugin_path] is set).

method.name: get_midi_output_driver
method.description: The driver the plugin's MIDI out plays through, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_parameter
method.description: Returns the current value of a parameter, in the plugin's own range (see [method get_parameters]).

method.name: get_parameter_modulation
method.description: The modulation offset [method set_parameter_modulation] set on parameter [param id], or 0.

method.name: get_parameter_text
method.description: Returns the plugin's own display text for a parameter's current value, such as [code]"-12.0 dB"[/code] or [code]"Large Hall"[/code]. Falls back to the plain number if the plugin provides no text.

method.name: get_parameters
method.description: Returns every parameter of the plugin, as a [Dictionary] with these keys: [code]id[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]module[/code] (a grouping such as [code]"Filter/Envelope"[/code]), [code]min[/code], [code]max[/code], [code]default[/code], [code]value[/code], [code]text[/code] (when the plugin provides one), [code]stepped[/code], [code]step_count[/code], [code]hidden[/code], [code]read_only[/code], and [code]property[/code] (the name of its inspector property).

method.name: get_plugin_info
method.description: Returns a description of the loaded plugin: [code]id[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]vendor[/code], [code]version[/code], [code]description[/code], [code]features[/code] (a [PackedStringArray] such as [code]["audio-effect", "reverb"][/code]), and [code]inputs[/code] and [code]outputs[/code], each an [Array] of ports with [code]name[/code], [code]channels[/code] and [code]main[/code]. A second input port is a sidechain (see [member sidechain]). Returns an empty [Dictionary] if no plugin is loaded.

method.name: get_presets
method.description: The presets the plugin offers, as a [Dictionary] each with [code]id[/code] (what [method load_preset] takes), [code]name[/code], [code]collection[/code] (a sound pack, may be empty), [code]creator[/code], [code]description[/code] and [code]tags[/code] (the plugin's own words: bass, pad ...). They come from the plugin's preset-discovery factory: presets built into it, and preset files in the folders it names (only those for this very plugin). Empty if it offers none. [b]Note:[/b] This may read every preset file the plugin names. Call it from a menu, not every frame.

method.name: is_editor_open
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the plugin's window is open.

method.name: is_learning
method.description: Whether [method learn_parameter] is waiting for a controller.

method.name: is_plugin_loaded
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the plugin at [member plugin_path] was found and loaded. If not, [method get_load_error] says why.

method.name: learn_parameter
method.description: MIDI learn: the next controller that moves (through [method midi_controller], which a [MidiInput] calls for its learners: [method MidiInput.add_learner]) is mapped to parameter [param id], replacing any mapping of that controller or that parameter. [signal midi_learned] then fires. [codeblock] input.add_learner(synth) synth.learn_parameter(synth.find_parameter("Cutoff")) # now turn a knob [/codeblock]

method.name: load_preset
method.description: Loads a preset from [method get_presets] by its [code]id[/code], into every instance of the plugin, so they all sound it at once. It then is the plugin's state: [member plugin_state] saves it with the scene, and values set by hand give way to it, as when a state is loaded. Returns [code]false[/code], with the reason printed, if the plugin refuses it.

method.name: map_controller
method.description: Maps controller [param controller] (0-127) on [param channel] (1-16) to parameter [param id], as learning would: its value 0-127 moves the parameter over its whole range, as a short ramp, so a knob glides rather than steps.

method.name: midi_controller
method.description: A controller moved, in MIDI 1.0 values: learned if [method learn_parameter] is waiting, then it moves the parameter it is mapped to. A [MidiInput] calls this for its learners; scripts can too.

method.name: midi_stop
method.description: A [MidiDriver] target method: withdraws transport changes from [param source] planned from [param time_us] on (a loop changed, say).

method.name: midi_transport
method.description: A [MidiDriver] target method: the driver's transport, as instruments get it (see [method MidiDriver.add_transport_target]). The plugin hears it as its transport, exact to the sample.

method.name: open_editor
method.description: Opens the plugin's own GUI in a window of its own, or brings it to the front if it is already open. Returns [code]false[/code] if it cannot open, with a warning saying why. The window stays open until it is closed by the user, by [method close_editor], or by the plugin, which emits [signal editor_closed]. Clicking an enabled effect on a bus in the Audio panel calls this. Works in the editor and in a running game, on Linux, Windows and macOS: a game can show a plugin's real interface (a synth's panel in a music app, say).

method.name: register_monitor
method.description: Shows [method get_dsp_load] in the editor's [b]Debugger > Monitors[/b] panel while the game runs, as [code]Plugins/<name> (DSP %)[/code], [param name] defaulting to the plugin's name. Removed again when this resource is freed, or with [method unregister_monitor].

method.name: scan_plugins
method.description: Returns every CLAP plugin found in [param extra_dirs] and the plugin folders (see the class description), as a [Dictionary] each with [code]path[/code], [code]id[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]vendor[/code], [code]version[/code], [code]description[/code] and [code]features[/code]. A file that could not be loaded is listed with [code]path[/code] and [code]error[/code] instead. Instruments are included (their [code]features[/code] contain [code]"instrument"[/code]); [method ClapInstrument.scan_plugins] lists only those. [b]Note:[/b] CLAP has no separate metadata files, so this loads every plugin binary to ask it. Call it from a menu, not every frame.

method.name: set_midi_output_driver
method.description: Plays the MIDI the plugin sends out (an arpeggiator's or chord generator's notes, see [signal midi_output]) through [param driver], a [MidiDriver]: on its channel targets, as its own notes (its stop and panic end them). [code]null[/code] for none. [codeblock] arp.set_midi_output_driver(second_midi) # the arp plays the instrument on second_midi's channel 1 arp.midi_output_latency_ms = 50.0 # optional: exact spacing [/codeblock]

method.name: set_parameter
method.description: Sets a parameter, in the plugin's own range (see [method get_parameters]); the value is clamped to that range. The change is heard one audio block (about 11.6 ms at 44.1 kHz) after the call, and changes keep their spacing in time exactly, so a value swept from [method Node._process] moves smoothly.

method.name: set_parameter_at
method.description: Like [method set_parameter], but heard [param delay] seconds later, placed to the exact sample. The stored value, and so the inspector, changes at once.

method.name: set_parameter_modulation
method.description: Moves parameter [param id] by [param amount] (in the parameter's own units, as [method get_parameters] gives them) on top of its set value, which stays as it is: the saved setting is untouched, the modulation lives only while the game runs. 0 ends it. CLAP parameters the plugin marks modulatable take it natively (CLAP_EVENT_PARAM_MOD, the plugin's own value and window unchanged); for any other, all of VST3 included, the host sends the value plus the offset, clamped to the range. Heard [param delay] seconds from now, sample-exact.

method.name: set_parameter_ramp
method.description: Glides parameter [param id] to [param value] over [param seconds], starting [param delay] seconds from now, sample-exact (a point every 32 samples, the last exactly [param value]): a filter opening as the player enters a cave, without zipper noise. The stored value, and the inspector, show [param value] at once. A ramp started while another glides on that parameter carries on from where it has got to; [method set_parameter] ends a ramp.

method.name: sync_beat
method.description: Puts the song position the plugin hears at [param beat] now (a downbeat, say), running on at [member bpm]: lines a beat-locked effect (a gate, a beat repeat) up with the music. Needs [member bpm] set.

method.name: unmap_parameter
method.description: Removes the mapping to parameter [param id].

method.name: unregister_monitor
method.description: Takes the monitor [method register_monitor] added out of the Monitors panel.

members.member: The tempo the plugin hears, for tempo-synced delays, LFOs, gates and arpeggiators: 0 (the default) gives it no tempo, as before. Set by anything (a game, GDSiON, gameplay), no driver needed; the song position runs on from the last [method sync_beat]. To follow a [MidiDriver] exactly instead (play, pause, loops, tempo maps), use [method MidiDriver.add_transport_target]. Saved with the scene.
The controller mappings (MIDI learn): [code]{"channel:controller": parameter id}[/code]. Saved with the scene, so a rig of knobs comes back with it.

For [method set_midi_output_driver]: 0 (the default) plays each forwarded event as soon as it reaches the main thread, up to an audio buffer and a frame late, unevenly. Above 0, each is due its own time plus this, so the spacing the plugin made is kept exactly; it must then be longer than the audio output buffer plus a frame (often 20-50 ms; the headless test driver needs about 150).

The parameters set by hand, as [code]{id: value}[/code]. Saved with the scene and applied after [member plugin_state] when it loads, so they win if the two disagree. Parameters not listed keep whatever the plugin holds: its default, or what a loaded state set. Not shown in the inspector, which shows one slider per parameter under [b]Parameters[/b] instead.

Which plugin to load, for a [code].clap[/code] file holding several: the plugin's id, such as [code]"michaelwillis.dragonfly.hall"[/code] (see [method scan_plugins]). Empty means the first plugin in the file. Changing it clears [member param_values] and [member plugin_state], since they belong to the previous plugin.

The [code].clap[/code] file to load. Usually relative to a plugin folder, such as [code]"DragonflyHallReverb.clap"[/code], which is what the Add Effect menu stores, so the scene works on other machines. An absolute path, or a [code]res://[/code] one, works too; an absolute path that does not exist falls back to its file name in the plugin folders. The plugin loads on the next frame, or as soon as something needs it. Changing it clears [member param_values] and [member plugin_state].

The plugin's complete state, as bytes only the same plugin can read: everything it needs to come back exactly as it was, which can be more than its parameters. Saved with the scene. Reading it asks the plugin for its current state. Setting it from a script loads a preset: it replaces every value set by hand so far ([member param_values]).

The name of a sidechain channel to feed into the plugin's second input, such as a ducking compressor's key input or a vocoder's carrier. Put a [ClapSidechainSend] with the same [member ClapSidechainSend.channel] on the bus whose sound should drive it. Empty for no sidechain; the plugin's second input then gets silence. [b]Note:[/b] Godot processes buses from the highest index down. If the source bus has a higher index than this effect's bus, the plugin hears the same audio block; otherwise one block (about 11.6 ms at 44.1 kHz) later.

How many ready-made plugin instances to keep for when Godot builds this effect's instances (adding the effect, changing the bus layout, or one per channel pair on surround buses). Godot does that while holding the audio lock, where creating a plugin could stall all audio for a few milliseconds; a spare is taken instantly instead. The default is [code]1[/code], enough for a stereo bus. With [code]0[/code], a new instance passes audio through unprocessed for a frame or two while its plugin is created. Each spare costs one plugin instance of memory, though no audio processing. Set [code]0[/code] for memory-hungry plugins, or more for surround buses (5.1 needs 3 instances, 7.1 needs 4).

signal.name: editor_closed
signal.description: Emitted when the plugin's window closes: by the user, by the plugin, or by [method close_editor].

signal.name: midi_learned
signal.description: [method learn_parameter] mapped a controller: [param channel] and [param controller] to parameter [param id].

signal.name: midi_output
signal.description: The plugin sent out a MIDI message (an arpeggiator's note, say): [param kind] a [enum MidiDriver.EventKind], [param channel] 1-16, [param index] the key or controller, [param value] at MIDI 2.0 resolution (velocity 16 bits, the rest 32), [param time_us] when it is heard, on [method MidiDriver.get_time_us]'s clock, exact to the sample. Emitted once a frame on the main thread, so up to an audio buffer and a frame after [param time_us]. From the first running instance only, so an effect Godot runs per channel pair does not report each note twice.

signal.name: parameter_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the plugin changes a parameter itself, for example from its own window. The new value is already stored in [member param_values] and sent to every instance.

signal.name: parameters_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the plugin's parameter list changes while it runs: names, ranges, or which parameters exist. Values for parameters that no longer exist are dropped, and the inspector is rebuilt.
